text:
jason: Heads up — while profiling runtime-gpu-3 this morning I saw steady RSS growth across a ~12h run when prefix cache reuse was enabled. Not a single huge leak, more like slow accumulation + fragmentation.

maya: ouch. is this when session-sticky is on?

jason: yes. sticky-affinity = user, we were reusing prefix keys across many short lived requests. When a session resets we still keep chunks in the shard until eviction kicks in. Eviction seems suboptimal for lots of small, overlapping prefixes.

li: any repro? logs or flamegraphs?

jason: attached flamegraph (summarized): lots of time in memcpy + allocator scanning during eviction. Heap snapshots show lots of 4k and 16k slabs that never get compacted. Also saw repeated small allocations for KV shards that were pinned by stale key references.

carlos: that matches what I saw on the 2-day load test — fragmentation increases with sequence length variance. When we route long-context clients to the same host, kernel selection switches to tiled attention which creates larger contiguous buffers, making small free fragments unusable.

emily: so two issues: keying / reuse strategy causing many distinct keys, and allocator fragmentation making eviction ineffective. any quick mitigation?

jason: a couple ideas: 1) normalize cache key to coarsen granularity for high-churn clients (prefix-fingerprint + bucketed-length). 2) add an adaptive TTL that decays faster for low-reuse prefixes. 3) opportunistic compaction on idle loops.

li: can you sketch the key change?

jason: current key: `kv::{model}:{session_id}:{prefix_token_count}:{prefix_hash}` (very high cardinality). Proposal: `kv::{model}:{prefix_fp}:{len_bucket}` where `prefix_fp = xxhash64(prefix_tokens)`, `len_bucket = floor(prefix_len / 64)` — this reduces distinct keys and increases reuse for similar prefixes. We keep session-scoped sticky maps only for pinned state (e.g., conversation metadata), not raw token prefixes.

maya: sounds reasonable. downsides: false positives on reuse (we may reuse slightly different prefixes) — but we can validate output-quality via a holdout eval set. Also need to ensure compatibility with routing fallback (we can't accidentally serve wrong KV to another model variant).

carlos: add `model_variant` to the key then: `kv::{model}:{model_variant}:{prefix_fp}:{len_bucket}`. Also track a cheap occlusion metric: last-used-ts and reuse-count to guide eviction order.

emily: what about memory growth from tiled kernels you mentioned? compaction alone might be slow. Could we prefer co-locating similar sequence-length workloads together or prefer kernel that uses smaller working set when memory pressure is high?

jason: yeah, idea: runtime can prefer small-ws kernels when host mem_util > 75%. Kernel selection policy already has latency/cost knobs; add a mem-pressure score that biases to lower working-set kernels even if token throughput drops slightly. That reduces fragmentation long-term.

li: for eviction heuristics: instead of pure LRU at key granularity, consider chunk-level LRU: keep contiguous KV chunk metadata and evict oldest chunks first so we can free large contiguous spans and reduce slab fragmentation.

carlos: chunk-level eviction + coarser keys + adaptive TTL seems like a good combo. We should A/B in staging with load tests that simulate many short chats.

jason: I'll prototype key schema + adaptive TTL in the cache layer today. Quick benchmark plan: baseline run with old keying, new keying, and new keying + chunk-eviction; 12h runs with churned prefixes and periodic long-context sessions. Metrics: RSS, fragmentation ratio (free-contiguous / total), eviction latency, tail p99 token latency.

emily: add a quality guard: sample 1% of requests and compare decoding outputs between old vs new keying; fail rollout if divergence rate > 0.2% on holdout prompts.

maya: +1 on the safety gate. also coordinate with infra for a canary host group. ops-bot: will create canary group + schedule the 12h jobs?

ops-bot: created canary group `kv-reuse-canary-1` and scheduled three 12h runs on runtime-gpu-3a,b,c starting 1782504800. Links: https://ci.internal/runs/3123

jason: thanks. i'll open a PR with the key schema and a small feature flag `kv_coarse_keying` so we can flip it in prod. Will also include metrics for reuse-rate and contiguous-free-space.

li: if you want, I can help with a mini allocator tweak to expose compaction hooks — might give a ~15% improvement in fragmentation on the benchmark.

jason: would love that. pairing later today.

carlos: logging note — make sure we don't spam logs for every key miss; emit counters only. Also tag metrics with `len_bucket` and `reusable=true|false` so we can do per-bucket analysis.

emily: sounds like a plan. once we have results we'll decide rollout. thanks team :thumbsup:
